title: Evaluating the Impact of Fertilizer Subsidy on Crop Yields

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Difference-in-Differences (DID). This method compares the change in crop yields before and after the subsidy implementation between treated (subsidy recipients) and control (non-recipients) farmers. The key assumption is parallel trends - that treated and control units would have followed similar yield trajectories in the absence of treatment. This allows us to isolate the causal effect of the fertilizer subsidy by differencing out time-invariant unit characteristics and common time trends.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s50_data.csv")

# Examine data structure
print("Data structure:")
print(head(data))
print(paste("Total observations:", nrow(data)))
print(paste("Unique units:", length(unique(data$unit_id))))
print(paste("Time periods:", length(unique(data$period))))

# Check treatment assignment
print("Treatment distribution:")
print(table(data$treated, data$post))

# Main DID regression
did_model <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = data)

# Print main results
print("=== MAIN DID RESULTS ===")
print(summary(did_model))

# Extract and highlight the treatment effect
treatment_effect <- coef(did_model)["treat_x_post"]
se_treatment <- sqrt(vcov(did_model)["treat_x_post", "treat_x_post"])
t_stat <- treatment_effect / se_treatment
p_value <- 2 * (1 - pt(abs(t_stat), df = did_model$df.residual))

print(paste("Treatment Effect (DID coefficient):", round(treatment_effect, 4)))
print(paste("Standard Error:", round(se_treatment, 4)))
print(paste("t-statistic:", round(t_stat, 4)))
print(paste("p-value:", round(p_value, 4)))

# Robustness check 1: Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors
robust_se <- sqrt(diag(vcovHC(did_model, type = "HC1")))
print("=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK 1: Robust Standard Errors ===")
print(paste("Treatment Effect:", round(treatment_effect, 4)))
print(paste("Robust Standard Error:", round(robust_se["treat_x_post"], 4)))
print(paste("Robust t-statistic:", round(treatment_effect / robust_se["treat_x_post"], 4)))

# Robustness check 2: Fixed effects specification
# Add unit fixed effects
data$unit_id <- factor(data$unit_id)
fe_model <- lm(y ~ unit_id + post + treat_x_post, data = data)

print("=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK 2: Unit Fixed Effects ===")
fe_treatment_effect <- coef(fe_model)["treat_x_post"]
fe_se <- sqrt(vcov(fe_model)["treat_x_post", "treat_x_post"])
print(paste("FE Treatment Effect:", round(fe_treatment_effect, 4)))
print(paste("FE Standard Error:", round(fe_se, 4)))

# Robustness check 3: Balance check - compare pre-treatment means
pre_treatment_data <- data[data$post == 0, ]
treated_pre_mean <- mean(pre_treatment_data$y[pre_treatment_data$treated == 1])
control_pre_mean <- mean(pre_treatment_data$y[pre_treatment_data$treated == 0])

print("=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK 3: Pre-treatment Balance ===")
print(paste("Pre-treatment mean (treated):", round(treated_pre_mean, 4)))
print(paste("Pre-treatment mean (control):", round(control_pre_mean, 4)))
print(paste("Pre-treatment difference:", round(treated_pre_mean - control_pre_mean, 4)))

# Summary of key findings
print("=== SUMMARY ===")
print(paste("Main DID Estimate:", round(treatment_effect, 4)))
print(paste("Interpretation: Fertilizer subsidy increased log yields by", 
            round(treatment_effect, 4), "units"))
print(paste("Percentage effect on yields: approximately", 
            round((exp(treatment_effect) - 1) * 100, 2), "%"))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive coefficient on the treatment interaction term (treat_x_post), likely in the range of 0.2 to 0.8, indicating that the fertilizer subsidy increases log crop yields. This translates to approximately 20-120% increase in yield levels. The positive effect is expected because fertilizers are key agricultural inputs that directly enhance soil nutrients and crop productivity, particularly beneficial for smallholder farmers who may be credit-constrained and unable to purchase optimal fertilizer quantities without subsidies. The magnitude should be economically significant given that fertilizer is often a binding constraint for smallholder agricultural productivity.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log crop yields over time between treated and untreated units.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The subsidy program significantly increased crop yields.
